Dodgy Publisher

By: Michael Duffett | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Con man publisher who destroys the hopes of aspirant writers who get nothing after parting between R20 000 and R30 000. He never pays any of his staff, 100's of complaints against him, police and private eyes are investigating him.

Summary:
Chis Smith who heads up Publishing World SA and Books Africa features on Hello Peter and other scam websites. Writers approach him ti have books published. he charges between R20 000 and R30 000 and mostly, if at all, writets recieve 10 copies and that is it, but they are tied into a really unfair contract. We expose that contract for what it is worth. he is always charging his address, he and his sister too in the business, never return calls and they never pay out royalties. When angry people do get to them, they say that their auditors will check what is outstanding. They duck snd dive.

Further information:
So this is a brief look into self publshing world and what to be aware of. Remarkably he never pays his staff. We plan to send in a researcher with an hidden camera to his premises - and we plan a confrontational interview. We will get three people who have been conned by him, and perhaps some collages of skype interviews of other writers he has conned, and of staff that have not been paid. We will get an attorney to talk about the contract and perhaps a real publisher who can talk how self publishing should be done.R

Extra Budget Items:
Shoot will happen in JHB 2 days. With presenter.. A 3rd day will be done by me in Cape Town at no cost.
Costs will be a flight first thing on Monday morning to JHB- a return flight. Will leave flight open in case I have to edit up there.
And hire of a car for two days. Two nights cheap hotel as we may go late into TUES evening.

Press Release:


Dashed Publishing Dreams
In a world of highly competitive new book sales, aspirant writers will go to great lengths to get their words into print and their books on the shelves. Some use publishing service companies to achieve their dreams. But one such company, a Gauteng-based publisher, seems to have pushed his clients just too far with unmet promises and a hefty price-tag that delivers too little. Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Michael Duffett
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Research: Siniketiwe Hlanze



Script:



Louis Lategan of Van Der Bijl Park has always been a keen writer.

Lategaan: it started as a hobby doing some short stories that occasionally did get publication in magazines.

He spent two years writing a book about a slice of life in the Vaal Triangle, and his manuscript was accepted by a publisher. SA is rich with untold stories and Louis had high hopes of his work being recognized:

Link. There must be 1000’s of writers and all of them have a story to tell. And all that they dream of is hitting the shelves of the major book stores in SA.

Mark: Not everyone can be published though the traditional channels, by the bigger publishes, but that should not stoop them in telling their stories.

Mark Hackney is CEO of a book marketing and distribution company. He has a selection of self published books which he distributes to major book stores. The authors have all edited their own manuscripts, designed the covers and printed their books. But, there is also another way.

Mark: Or they can also contract a publishing service company, who can do that all on their behalf.

Link: a number of new and aspirant writers have put their faith in a small publishing company Publishing World SA only to have their dreams dashed.

And that’s the company Louis Lategan put his faith into way back in 2016.

Lategaan: What I have is the sample back and front page, for R21850.

That’s all he received - two and a half years after signing his contract.

Louis is not alone. Another exasperated writer is retired professor gert maritz who spent two years drawing on his vast experience, to write a book called My Health – are my grand parents to blame?

Maritz: you must imagine that when you write a book on a topic like this and its your first book, then you have some expectations.

Expectations he says were never met, In 2016 he signed a contract with publishing world SA and paid R37800. A sample book arrived a year later, full of mistakes. He painstakingly corrected them and sent them back to Publishing world SA.

Maritz: Then in April 2018 I got another book, full of errors, actually new errors.



Twice publishing world sa got the titles of the book wrong. Grand parents on the front covers, grand parent on the spines.

Another unhappy client is Esmeraldo Meyer. Her dreams of becoming a pilot were dashed when she lost her sight in one eye in a freak accident. But a new passion developed

Esmeraldo: After that I just started writing, its just being given to me, I woke up one night and I just found the title of my book.

At the age of 18 she completed a story of a young woman who could not come to terms with her parent’ murder. She paid publishing world SA R25 000. She is upset because it took almost 2 years for her to receive ten copies of her book which she said were of poor quality.


Esmeraldo: I feel very disappointed because In worked hard for this - it was a very big achievement for me,

Chris Smith, who started Publishing world SA, and who also has another company BooksAfrica, agreed to meet with us to respond to allegations. He described why he started Publishing World SA



Chris: I wanted to start a publishing house to help new authors, authors that just started, no one wants to help them, they are unknown.

Presenter: So what do you do?

Chris: The complete publishing process, if their manuscript was accepted, the design of the cover, getting registration numbers, a fully editing process, the proof reading, the layout, and the printing of ten books which must go to the authors, sometimes 30.

The cost will depend on the size, length and complexity of each book.

The Publishing world sa contract gives the company exclusive rights to produce publish and sell author’s book for 3 years or until 1000 have been sold. The authors will receive 10 free books. It encourages writers to assist in their own marketing and Publishing world SA can’t guarantee sales through its networks.. Smith says he has tried a variety of marketing approaches . which still includes holding book launches for authors

A book launch is furthest from `Louis Lategan’s mind who signed his contract in 2016.


Presenter: he paid you though 21850 but this is all that he got.

Chris: ya, that don’t seem to be right. The Arthur’s once they pay they get a contract to then they get a copy of the contract,

Presenter: What do they pay for?

Chris:: they pay for a full publication process

Louis never got that at all. His emails to publishing world all bounced back.

Chris: if his books are not finished, then we don’t have a problem finishing them.

Louis is not holding out much hope though.

Luois: I have given up

The professor too is almost ready to give up .

Presenter: What about Professor Maritz. All he got was two sample books in almost three years.

Chris: So he has two proof books, he was supposed to go through that, and he was supposed to send through if he was happy, then they will deliver the ten books to him.

The Professor said that he was so dismayed at the number of mistakes in the 2nd book that he simply sent it back and said – reedit. Then he could not get hold of publishing world SA..

Maritz: I tried several times on email, even phoned.

Louis: my cell phone number, I have it for 20 years – never changed my cell phone number, my cell no was up everywhere.

Then there is the question of royalites. This is John Galbraith’s contract which he signed in 2015 with Publishing World SA to have his book, the Last Rhino, published. He paid in R21500. A book launch was held in 2016.

John: at my book launch I sold more than 50 books ….I to date have not received one cent of commission from Publishing world SA.

Chris, however, questions the number of books sold though.

Chris. We must get all the figures from the printers

He said that he had actually asked a firm of accountants to look into the sales figures.

Presenter: can we contact that company

Chris: well we did ask them to do it but they never did.

Link: it is just writers that are upset with chris smith. Its also former staff members and former partners in his book stores franchises. They have raised concern and are angry:

Like Susan Sieberhagen who was seduced by the opportunity of becoming a book store owner..

Chris offered a fully equipped multi purpose book shop which would be ready by the 4 of Jan 2017.

Susan: I realized that this is what I wanted to do I wanted to work for my self.

She paid in R150 000 for a joint directorship but come the 4th of Jan, she said the store was not ready.

Susan: he promised a fully equipped stores, and I did not get it.

Chris: For the space that was available there, it was a fully equipped store.

Susan said had to find extra money to finish the store.

Susan: R150 000 but to finish the store, more than R250,000.

She added that `Chris offered her R6500 per month salary. He denied that.

Chris: She was running the business, she was a partner, she must establish her own salary, that is ridiculous.

And He accused her of theft.

`Susan vehemently denies this. She says she used the stores credit card to pay the Telkom account. Susan lasted a few months before she walked out and found another job. She is seeking legal advice to try and reclaim costs for promises not delivered.

Chris told us that all the franchisee stores had shut down, and that he now was creating websites for authors where customers can buy their books directly. Authors will pay Books Africa to distribute and Their books will also appear on the Books Africa website.

In the mean time the professor is still fuming because his book is now out of date

Professor: when `I submitted it in 2016 it was up to date. Now with new research, its out of date.

Chris claims that more than 70% of authors books did see the light. He urges unhappy clients to get hold of him.

Chris: their cases must be resolved, we will still publish their books and make their dreams come true.

We expose that contract for what it is worth. he is always charging his address, he and his sister too in the business, never return calls and they never pay out royalties. When angry people do get to them, they say that their auditors will check what is outstanding. They duck snd dive.
metadata.Further information: So this is a brief look into self publshing world and what to be aware of. Remarkably he never pays his staff. We plan to send in a researcher with an hidden camera to his premises - and we plan a confrontational interview. We will get three people who have been conned by him, and perhaps some collages of skype interviews of other writers he has conned, and of staff that have not been paid. We will get an attorney to talk about the contract and perhaps a real publisher who can talk how self publishing should be done.R

metadata.Viewing Notes: Viewing: The Dodgy Publisher Insert Producer: Michael Duffet Executive Producer: Wynand Grobler Managing Editor: Anna-Maria van Niekerk Supervising producer: Chwayitisa Futshane Social Media: Mnet: Tim du Plessis Legal: Nozipho Mngomezulu WG comments: Boring -- feels very long -- doesn’t build up the drama nicely Must explain what the SA publishing scene is like...must explain better Upfront – tell us more about the publishing world and what you should expect to get when you pay R20k Don’t start with Esmeraldo Maybe start with the professor he wrote something more legit and he is credible We need to know how they are ripped and what was promised for the R21k and what did they not get. If you’re self-publishing, with your risk, what does that actually mean. Have you been ripped When you go to Chris – the outside of the building is quite crummy – REMOVE You need to also hear Macfarlanes question to him to hear his response We don’t ask him about the marketing that Esmeralda expected ie. book launch.. We got into Chris too quickly and we haven’t established all the issues around It doesn’t feel like a confront with Chris – do we not have any establishing shots of them Royalties – we don’t explain what the royalties mean, what percentage are we talking about – has he even sold any books General context upfront Structure is wrong Louis is not holding his breath – bad scripting Mac audio??? You need to write a better script – this script is pedestrian LEGAL Nicely balanced “For BEE purposes” -- is not clear what this means Esmeralda’s allegations are not answered Royalties not clear -- we don’t know how much was LEGAL use this in script – “The contract says he is entitled to royalties and not withstanding that he sold 500 books, he hasn’t received any royalties” BEE – we don’t properly explain what this actually means Contract terms – we must be mindful of making too much of the contract because they were not duped into signing the contract which is not unfavourable to them
